Exact comparison: for f(z)=z^(N-r)p(z), f(q^j)=sum_k p_k(q^(N-r+k))^j. The nonzero terms give a reduced simple-pole generating series; with T=r,D=N the supplied q meets Algorithm 4 order>=max(D,2T). Coefficients are already supplied. A one-monomial f can have operator rank r or 1, so scalar recovery is not the requested action. Projection, short transforms, full decoding and N outputs remain paid. Massey 1969 §II eq(2), §IV Theorem 4/corollary, pp122,125–126: https://www.isiweb.ee.ethz.ch/archive/massey_pub/pdf/BI411.pdf ; van der Hoeven–Lecerf 2024 §5 Algorithm 4/eq(10), pp13–14: https://www.texmacs.org/joris/ffsparse/ffsparse.pdf. [2026-10-16; named primary-source comparison complete]
Exact comparison: e0,R e0,…,R^(N-1)e0 form a basis because R is a nonzero weighted cycle; invertible H gives the same for H R^j e0. Thus minpoly(R)=minpoly(D)=z^N−1 and the full vector orbit needs common scalar recurrence order N. The raw scalar projection e0^T R^j e0 has series 1/(1-z^N) and all N q-grid modes, despite one-sparse coordinate states. Special projections may cancel; no circuit lower bound follows. Massey 1969 §II eq(2), §IV Theorem 4/corollary, pp122,125–126: https://www.isiweb.ee.ethz.ch/archive/massey_pub/pdf/BI411.pdf ; van der Hoeven–Lecerf 2024 §5 Algorithm 4/eq(10), pp13–14: https://www.texmacs.org/joris/ffsparse/ffsparse.pdf. A T=N invocation of that algorithm needs order>=2N, beyond the supplied q; known-grid N-point recovery remains possible and paid.
